title: Kafka Consumer Lag (M15)
description: Per-group per-topic consumer lag, built entirely on the kafka-exporter metrics infra/compose already scrapes (M2) - no new exporter or principal needed. See infra/compose/README.md's M15 section for which metric backs each panel.

panels.title: Total lag, all groups (records behind)
panels.description: sum(kafka_consumergroup_lag) - the single number that answers "is anything falling behind, anywhere".

panels.title: Lag by consumer group (summed across topics and partitions)
panels.description: sum by (consumergroup) (kafka_consumergroup_lag) - one bar per consumer group (payment-api.replies.*, psp-connector, ledger.v1, webhook-notifier.*, analytics-streams.v1, analytics.status-audit-batch.v1, realtime-gateway.*, connect-mongo-audit-sink - docs/diagrams/topic-map.md's consumer-groups table).

panels.title: Consumer groups reporting (kafka-exporter's own visibility)
panels.description: count(count by (consumergroup) (kafka_consumergroup_lag)) - a sanity check on the exporter itself: if this drops to 0 while services are running, kafka-exporter's Describe-only ACL or its scrape is broken, not the consumers (M14's 'reports healthy and moves nothing' trap, one layer up the metrics pipeline).

panels.title: Lag by group and topic, over time
panels.description: sum by (consumergroup, topic) (kafka_consumergroup_lag) - the panel this dashboard exists for: per-group PER-TOPIC lag, watchable live. A group consuming more than one topic (psp-connector: payments.payment-requested.v1 + refunds.funds-reserved.v1 + psp.provider-status-query.v1) gets one line per topic, not one blended line.

panels.title: Lag by partition (detail - watch this during a lag-induction drill)
panels.description: kafka_consumergroup_lag{consumergroup,topic,partition} unaggregated - the same metric panel 4 sums, kept at full partition granularity for M19-style drills (kill a consumer instance, watch its partitions' lag climb; restart it, watch recovery).

panels.title: Consumer group current offset by topic (context for the lag panels above)
panels.description: sum by (consumergroup, topic) (kafka_consumergroup_current_offset) - lag alone doesn't say whether a group is stuck or just behind a fast producer; this shows whether the offset is advancing at all.
